name: Sled Push
description: The sled push is a linear strength and conditioning exercise in which the athlete drives a loaded sled forward across a surface by pushing from handles at the rear, maintaining a forward lean with straight arms. The hip extension and leg drive mechanics closely replicate the acceleration phase of sprinting, making it a highly effective training tool for sport-specific linear power, lower body strength development, and high-intensity metabolic conditioning with minimal eccentric muscle damage.

execution.starting_position: Stand behind the sled, gripping the upright handles. Lean forward at approximately 45 degrees, arms straight.
execution.setup_instructions: Load the sled appropriately — heavier loads develop strength, lighter loads develop speed and conditioning. Use a rubber or turf surface for most sled work.
steps: Step 1: Grip the sled handles and lean forward with the body at roughly 45 degrees and arms straight.
Step 2: Drive off one foot, pushing forcefully into the floor, as the other leg swings through.
Step 3: Maintain short, powerful strides — stay on the balls of the feet, never the heels.
Step 4: Keep the hips down and avoid raising the torso — the lean angle is maintained throughout.
Step 5: Drive the sled forward for the prescribed distance, maintaining consistent force output.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe rhythmically throughout. Exhale with each leg drive.
common_mistakes: Letting the arms bend — straight arms transfer force more efficiently to the sled
Pushing with the toes instead of the full foot drive
Standing too upright — reduces horizontal force vector on the sled
safety_considerations: Ensure the surface is appropriate — asphalt can damage sled bases not designed for it.
Adequate lower body warm-up before heavy sled work.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip and knee extension on each stride.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Typically performed for distance (20–40 meters). Heavy: slow and powerful. Light: fast and explosive.
coaching_cues: Stay low — maintain the forward lean
Drive the foot into the ground
Arms straight — push through the handles
